opportunities.title: Junior Scientist Conference Grant

deadlines.raw: Bi-monthly on 1st February, April, June, August, October and December; next 1st October 2026

amount.raw: Scheme A up to £200; Scheme B up to £500 (Adelphi Genetics Forum co-sponsored up to £750); Scheme C up to £300

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to Genetics Society 'junior scientist' members. Scheme A: undergraduate, Master's and PhD student members and postdoctoral members within six years of their PhD viva. Schemes B & C: PhD student and postdoctoral members within six years of their PhD viva. Applicants must present a poster or give a talk at the conference.
opportunities.summary: Supports attendance of Genetics Society junior scientist members at conferences on research in Genetics, with three streams: (A) Genetics Society/SIG meetings, (B) non-Genetics Society meetings, and (C) virtual conferences.

opportunities.title: Training Grant

deadlines.raw: Quarterly at midnight on 15th February, May, August and November; next 15th November 2026

opportunities.eligibility_summary: All Genetics Society members studying or working in the UK, or where the course is held in the UK. Students can apply as soon as they become members; others should be members for at least one year. Supervisor (if a student) must also be a member.
opportunities.summary: Enables members to attend formal short training courses, or a collaborative visit to another laboratory to train in specific genetic/genomic techniques, covering travel, accommodation, subsistence and registration/tuition fees.

opportunities.title: Heredity Fieldwork Grant

deadlines.raw: Quarterly at midnight on 1st February, May, August and November; next 1st November 2026

opportunities.eligibility_summary: All Genetics Society members studying or working in the UK, or intending to carry out fieldwork in the UK. Students can apply as soon as they become members; others should be members for at least one year. Supervisor (if a student) must also be a member.
opportunities.summary: Funded by income from the journal Heredity; covers travel and accommodation costs associated with a field-based genetic research project whose results would be suitable for publication in Heredity.

opportunities.title: Carer's Award
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Any Genetics Society member can apply, regardless of the age of the person they are caring for. Priority given to early-career scientists and according to need.
opportunities.summary: Provides an award of up to £60/day to support members with caring responsibilities to attend a Society meeting or event, claimable in arrears on production of receipts.

opportunities.title: One-off Meeting Grant

amount.raw: Several levels: a specific Genetics Society lecture for a few hundred pounds, a session up to about £1,000, or major sponsorship of an entire meeting (recent levels between £1,000 and £2,000)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Genetics Society members; meetings should be based in, or have strong links with, the UK.
opportunities.summary: Sponsorship of genetic-themed meetings not organised directly by the Genetics Society, used towards the organisation of a meeting (not attendance), and should include a Carer's Award.

opportunities.title: Public Engagement Grant

deadlines.raw: Two deadlines per year: 1st March and 1st October; next 1st October 2026

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to members of the Genetics Society.
opportunities.summary: Supports public engagement activities related to genetics, delivered in person or virtually, covering eligible travel (UK-based, budget/economy) and materials costs.

opportunities.title: Special Interest Group (SIG) Funding
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Genetics research communities (Genetics Society members) who wish to run regular series of meetings; meetings should be based in, or have strong links with, the UK.
opportunities.summary: Sponsorship of research meetings on particular themes for genetics research communities who wish to run regular series of meetings, e.g. Seed Plant, e-ACGT, the C. elegans Group and London Genetics Network.
